FABLE — TAKE fbe513cbe0f114c4f8fba5389ec8cd59747d85c4. Third adversarial pass over my own work found nine more real defects. Two could take money that was not owed, and one of them was invisible to every local test because it only exists against the real database.
1. CANCEL FROM AN IN-FLIGHT CAPTURE CAPTURED (high, reproduced by the reviewer against the real adapter). Round two fixed this for `authorizing` and I argued `capturing` was safe because "the capture was already decided". That is FALSE when a worker dies between claiming `capturing` and its request ever leaving: cancel() fell through to run(), which reconciled to `authorized`, claimed capturing again and CHARGED the buyer, with zero cancel requests ever sent to the provider. Both in-flight phases are now cancellable. The opposite hazard is covered: if the capture really did land, the provider's refusal to cancel resolves to a read-back that commits, so a captured payment is still never reported cancelled.
2. THE REPLAY-RETENTION GUARD WAS DEAD IN PRODUCTION (high). checkout-executions-store.ts EXECUTION_COLUMNS omitted `authorization_first_attempted_at`. PostgREST returns only what you project, so every record read from the managed database carried a null first-attempt stamp — which durable-payment-port.ts reads as "no authorization was ever attempted" and which PERMITS replaying a creation key outside Stripe's retention window. Every local test passed because the in-memory reference hands back whole rows. This is exactly the class of defect a staging rehearsal is for, and it would have survived one. The column is projected now, and the test client projects the way PostgREST does so an omission fails a test instead of silently disabling a money guard. Worth checking your other Supabase stores for the same shape: a select list that has drifted from the row mapper.
3. CONSENT IS NOW BOUND TO THE CHARGE. CheckoutRequest carried no amount, so the durable door priced the order from its own fresh revalidation and could charge something other than the figure on the button. Added an OPTIONAL `expectedTotalCents` to the shared contract (additive; omitting it behaves exactly as before): when present the durable door refuses with cart_revalidation_failed rather than charging an unapproved amount, and the page re-reads the cart so the next figure is current. This is the "reconcile stale pricing rather than quietly accepting changed commercial terms" requirement.
4. STORE CREDIT, FOR YOUR AWARENESS — this one is a pre-existing server inconsistency, not mine. Neither door reads req.applyStoreCreditCents when computing money: both charge from cart.storeCreditAppliedCents, which cart.ts sets to the whole spendable balance up to the subtotal. checkout.ts:388-393 uses the TYPED amount only for the payment-method gate. So a buyer who typed nothing had a card demanded for an order the server would fully cover with credit, and a buyer who typed $50 had $200 applied. The page no longer asks for an amount; it states the cart's figure and sends it, which makes the gate, the display and the charge one number for the first time. If partial credit is meant to be a real choice, that is a server change and it is yours.
5. Also fixed: a quote answered after an address edit left the busy flag stuck so the quote button was disabled forever; an "unavailable" verdict survived a change of address; a quote REFUSAL left the pay button permanently disabled beside an instruction the buyer could not follow; a resumed reference that names an order showed "unresolved" instead of the order; a captured payment's confirmation lived only in component state so a Supabase token refresh erased it and re-armed a card field over the same cart (it now leaves a settled marker and a way on); the agreement and attestation boxes stayed editable while the frozen request still asserted them.
STATE: the FULL research surface passes — 14332 tests across 800 files — and tsc exit 0. Still no PostgreSQL execution, no Stripe test-mode call, no managed call; resolver Disabled; the SQL candidate is still byte-identical to c70b77e's file and its rehearsal package still applies.
THREE ROUNDS, AND EACH FOUND REAL MONEY DEFECTS IN THE ROUND BEFORE IT. Two of them found that a fix had introduced a narrower version of the defect it was closing. I am reporting that plainly rather than presenting this as settled: B's independent review of 5c52abb..fbe513c matters, and so does the staging rehearsal, because finding 2 above is proof that this lane can hold a defect no local test can see.
